title: Bram and the Group Chat
premise: Elodie Halloran has spent twelve years being the careful new kid, moving schools after an accident she refuses to talk about. When her grandmother's recipe box yields instructions written for something other than cooking, she discovers the school was built over a sealed covenant — and the group chat that keeps it, 'Bram,' has been waiting twelve years for her to answer a summons she never knew existed. Pulled into a hidden society of students bound by inherited duty, Elodie must choose between the safe, label-free life she's built and claiming her grandmother's role as the covenant's keeper. When the seal begins to fail before prom and the price of renewal is a memory or a life, Elodie rewrites the terms herself, ending the inheritance cycle at the cost of her own place in Bram — walking out of prom unbound, finally free to be someone without a label.
about_author: C. M. Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former small-town librarian who grew up above a shuttered grange hall and never stopped wondering what was under the floorboards. They write young adult fiction about kids who inherit more than furniture.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Unpacking in her aunt's attic, Elodie finds her late grandmother's recipe box and a card that reads like directions for a ritual, not dinner. A text from an unknown number arrives: 'You're late.' The beat is quiet dread — the careful life she's constructed just cracked.

chapters.title: Ashford Prep Sits on Something
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. First week at Ashford Prep; she maps exits, memorizes social hierarchies, notices the school's foundation stones are older than the town. A boy named Wren watches her too knowingly. Emotional beat: hypervigilance disguised as confidence.

chapters.title: Six Unread Messages
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. We meet Bram, the six-student group chat that maintains the covenant beneath the school. Wren reports that the seventh seat — the Keeper — has pinged active for the first time in twelve years. Beat: reluctant hope that the burden might finally shift.

chapters.title: Instructions Not for Food
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Following the recipe card literally — salt at the north door, a spoken name — Elodie witnesses the hallway breathe. She runs. Beat: terror braided with a shameful thrill of belonging to something.

chapters.title: The Terms of Inheritance
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren intercepts Elodie before she can transfer out, laying out the truth: her grandmother was Keeper, the accident twelve years ago happened the night the seal weakened, and the seat passes by blood whether she accepts or not. Beat: fury at a legacy chosen for her.

chapters.title: Labels
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. At lunch, Elodie catalogues the labels she's worn — orphan, weirdo, new kid — and realizes Bram offers one more: Keeper. She attends her first meeting as an observer only. Beat: guarded curiosity winning over flight.

chapters.title: What the Seal Costs
chapters.summary: Priya's POV, a senior Bram member. Priya shows Elodie what maintenance takes: each member pays annually in memories, and Priya can no longer recall her brother's face. Beat: grief as warning — this is what Elodie would inherit.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Careful
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Flashback chapter: the night of the accident, her grandmother's last phone call, why Elodie stopped trusting herself. She realizes her caution wasn't cowardice but training she never consented to. Beat: reframing shame as preparation.

chapters.title: Hairline Fracture
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. During a routine check, the seal cracks visibly — three months early. Bram scrambles; the renewal rite requires the Keeper's blood and choice, and Elodie is the only candidate. Beat: panic compressing the timeline.

chapters.title: Prom Committee and Other Doomsdays
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Comic-relief chapter: Elodie gets roped into prom committee with outsider friend Dev, a normal life pulling at her even as Bram texts escalate. Beat: longing for an ordinary adolescence she can't have.

chapters.title: The Archive Under the Gym
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Wren shows her the covenant archive; Elodie finds her grandmother's journals and learns the previous Keeper tried to renegotiate the terms and failed, paying everything. Beat: hope and horror in equal measure.

chapters.title: Training Montage, Badly
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Bram trains Elodie in the rites; she's clumsy, defiant, asks forbidden questions. Wren softens toward her; Priya warns him not to. Beat: first warmth of found family — which makes the coming cost crueler.

chapters.title: What Wren Owes
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Reveal: Wren's family has served Bram for four generations; his older sister paid the memory-price at seventeen and no longer knows him. He needs Elodie to accept so no one else's sibling is next. Beat: love entangled with duty.

chapters.title: The Interim Rite
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. To stabilize the crack, Bram performs a stopgap rite using Elodie's blood without full Keeper authority. It works — and something on the other side now knows her name. Beat: power gained, attention earned.

chapters.title: Dev Asks the Wrong Question
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev notices Elodie disappearing, finds salt lines and burn marks, and demands answers. Elodie lies badly. Beat: the cost of secrecy — the ordinary life fraying exactly when she needs it.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Deciphering the final journal page, Elodie learns the truth of the accident: her grandmother broke the seal deliberately to save child-Elodie, and the renewal price has been accruing interest ever since. Beat: guilt transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Bram ensemble POV, rotating. The entity beneath offers new terms: full renewal if the Keeper gives a whole life-memory — effectively erasing Elodie's identity — or the old terms: one member's memories per year, forever. Beat: the trap of fair-sounding bargains.

chapters.title: The Night Before Prom
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie drafts her acceptance, says quiet goodbyes to her aunt and Dev, and dances alone in her room in the dress she'll never wear properly. Wren arrives with a confession he can't finish. Beat: tender, doomed calm.

chapters.title: Prom, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Mid-prom, the seal fails outright; the gym floor splits along old foundation lines. Bram mobilizes in formalwear while Dev, refusing to be shut out, follows Elodie down. Beat: chaos, courage, the two worlds colliding.

chapters.title: The Bargaining Floor
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. In the chamber beneath, Elodie faces the entity and rejects both sets of terms. Drawing on her grandmother's failed renegotiation and twelve years of careful observation, she proposes a third option: a covenant paid in witnessed remembrance rather than sacrifice. Beat: the climax — wit and will against inherited law.

chapters.title: When the Labels Come Off
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The rite succeeds: the entity accepts, the debt dissolves, and Bram's members begin recovering stolen memories — including Wren's sister saying his name. But the Keeper's seat is spent; Elodie walks free and unbound. Beat: triumph shadowed by loss.

chapters.title: A Recipe for Ordinary
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Graduation-adjacent epilogue: Elodie writes her own card for the empty recipe box — directions for living, not sealing — and mails copies to Bram. Dev drags her back onto the dance floor at the rescheduled prom. Final beat: she chooses who to be, with no label required.
